reader_question: How much does the federal government collect each year?
title: Federal receipts reached $5.40 trillion in fiscal year 2026, up from $3.25 trillion in 2015.
measure_line: Federal receipts, billions of dollars not adjusted for inflation, fiscal years 2015 to 2026, the years the Treasury table we drew holds; each fiscal year ends September 30
source_line: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement, Table 9, receipts by source, fiscal 2015 to 2026, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Nominal dollars, not adjusted for inflation.
alt: Twelve years of federal receipts as columns at full width and as bars on a phone. Both rise from 3,249 billion dollars in 2015 to 5,403 billion in 2026, with a fall in 2023.

table.caption: Federal receipts by fiscal year, billions of dollars

phone_note: On a phone the twelve columns turn into bars, so every value keeps its label.
